The home perch. Detection reads the live kernel through the crowned manager.
The Next perch. Same wire protocol as KernelSU — told apart only by the Next-only probes (hook mode, version tag, manager app id).

The elder perch. Magisk is a boot-time root system: without a Magisk-patched boot image there is detection only, no live control. Presence here means the magisk binary answered in a root shell — not that its daemon runs.
The patch perch. APatch speaks a different tongue (supercall + SuperKey) — no probe is wired in Phase 1, so this perch reports honestly instead of guessing.
The wild perch. BakaSU shares the KernelSU wire protocol, so a BakaSU kernel reads as KernelSU-family above; no BakaSU-specific probe is wired in Phase 1.
